articleTitle: Modelling multiplexed speech and video VBR networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: Multiplex models for speech and video signals have been designed and have been found to be consistent in that the state probabilities obtained as a result of the transition probabilities agree closely with the state probabilities calculated directly by aggregation of the channel models. The authors have endeavoured to produce multiplex simulation models to represent any combination of speech and video channels. When such models are added to a single observation channel, the effects of impairments caused by temporary over load peaks can be reproduced and the users' reactions investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ATM network components-the service access switch and the link multiplexer
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: The authors describe the customer needs that can be satisfied by ATM networks and the 'road-map' showing how current and emerging networks are like to evolve to a full and potentially global B-ISDN offering. They break down the network requirements for such an offering into specific network components and detail how such components are being investigated at BTRL (British Telecom Research Laboratories). The current status of ATM worldwide, market drivers and the evolution towards ATM networks have been briefly reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: Asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) performance management is concerned with the network management and control functions that relate to the quantitative behaviour (performance) of ATM networks. An important objective of performance management is to ensure that the network is able to maintain required quality of service (QOS) levels efficiently. The requirements for service integration and a guaranteed high QOS imply that a high level of performance management capabilities must be embedded in the network. The author discusses specific, important aspects of ATM performance management and describes current thinking within the BT (British Telecom) on these subjects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: The CCITT has already agreed that ATM is the target transfer mode for future broadband networks and the author considers possible introduction strategies for such networks, the description being based on work within the largest project in the European Commission RACE programme: R1022 Technology for ATD. An architecture appropriate for an ATM multiservice network has been outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: Fast packet switching is a technique for switching traffic for a wide variety of services ranging from short text message interchange to complex real-time multi-media conferences. The technique draws ideas from both packet and circuit switching, and thus brings together the areas of data communication and telecommunications. The author describes the evolution of the ISDN, options for broadband switching architectures and fast packet switching architectures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: Asynchronous transfer mode has been selected by CCITT as the universal bearer for broadband ISDN services. The author briefly reviews the characteristics of ATM concentrating on the aspects which will be apparent to potential users of B-ISDN. The European Commission RACE programme focuses research and development on integrated broadband communications which includes terminal systems and applications as well as B-ISDN network capabilities. The application pilots within RACE are outlined and conclusions drawn on the relevance of ATM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: A prototype network, the Fairisle network, provides dedicated links to a workstation with a line rate of the order of 100 Mbit/s. These links are interconnected through a mesh of fast packet switches (FPS). The network provides an infrastructure for end-to-end cell delivery over which one or more transport protocols can operate. Transport protocols for a multiservice network such as Fairisle are discussed. The requirements of different types of user-service are described. Differences in these requirements, in terms of the transfer of user information, point to the adoption of a range of transport protocols. The author has identified the management of transport connections as a particular problem that has received less attention to date. An architecture for connection management that is appropriate for all services is described. He concludes with some pointers towards future developments in this area.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Packet Switching
abstract: The IEEE 802.6 standard defines an integrated services MAN technology based on a shared medium access protocol, suitable for several applications within a metropolitan area network. The author gives an overview of the IEE 802.6 protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
